title: Cyclotomic $L$-value decomposition — verification, $N=5$ instance, and analytic-number-theory bridge
html:
This note records the numerical verification, the N = 5 instance, the analytic-number-theory bridge, the Catalan-constant (n=2) instance, and cross-references for prop:cyclotomic-l-value-decomposition.

Numerical verification at 50 dps

cl_n_l_value_decomposition.py, witness:

Quantity Value (50 dps)
\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(i) (closed form \pi^3/32) 0.96894614625937036181867968128\ldots
\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(i) (direct polylog) 0.96894614625937036181867968128\ldots
\beta(3) (classical closed form) same
Residual 0 (exact match)

N = 5 instance (Theorem G dim (K - 3)/2 = 1)

Cyclotomic depth-3 content over \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5):

  • \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) \approx 0.18937
  • \mathrm{Cl}_3(4\pi/5) \approx -0.76636
  • Genuinely-new generator = \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) - \mathrm{Cl}_3(4\pi/5) \approx 0.95572

Corresponds, via the Hurwitz–Lerch decomposition, to the 2 odd Dirichlet characters \chi_5, \chi_5^3 mod 5 (complex-conjugate pair). Modulo bar-conjugation: 1 real dimension. Matches Theorem G.

Bridge to analytic number theory

The graded-Mikusiński framework's depth-n cyclotomic content IS the Dirichlet L-value content at integer n, up to \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K)-linear combinations. Three consequences follow:

  1. Classical L-value identities are theorems of our framework: \beta(3) = \pi^3/32, \beta(5) = 5\pi^5/1536, etc., all follow from Theorem A as instances.
  2. Conversely: any new theorem we prove about cyclotomic depth-n structure (e.g., Theorem D dimension) gives a corresponding statement about Dirichlet L-values.
  3. Beilinson's conjecture at \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K) depth n is the Beilinson conjecture on L-values of Dirichlet characters — a classical open problem now reframed within this framework.

Catalan's constant (n = 2 instance)

For (n, K) = (2, 4) even case: Theorem A gives \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(i) = -\pi^2/48 (Bernoulli B_2(1/4) = -1/48, times \pi^2 \cdot 2! / 2 = \pi^2). And \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(i) = \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/2) = G — Catalan's constant.

G is not Tate-rational (conjecturally transcendental); it's the genuinely-new depth-2 generator over \mathbb{Q}(i). Matches Theorem G: (K - 1)/2 = (4 - 1)/2 — but K = 4 is not prime; for prime K = 3: dim 1 = \mathrm{Cl}_2(2\pi/3) (Gieseking).
